title: Proofs 3–4: nothing greater than God; first being contains all perfection
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): THIRD, that God extensively plus intensively infinite is thus I prove. For every finite being something else more perfect plus greater can be. For God nothing more perfect plus greater can be. Therefore God a finite being is not. FOURTH, God every perfection belonging toward being has, because ye absolute first, on which all ye rest depend, necessarily by His perfection all remaining beings exceeds. Therefore every perfection belonging toward theirs in Himself in a more eminent manner He contains, plus powers which never so exhausted can be that new species plus perfections belonging toward things they cannot bring forth.
pass_b_english: THIRD, I prove that God is extensively and intensively infinite thus. For every finite being something else can be more perfect and greater. For God nothing can be more perfect and greater. Therefore God is not a finite being.

FOURTH, God has every perfection of being, because the absolute first, on which all the rest depend, necessarily exceeds all remaining beings by His perfection. Therefore He contains every perfection of theirs in Himself in a more eminent manner, and powers which can never be so exhausted that they cannot bring forth new species and perfections of things.
source_text: TERTIO, Deum extensive & intensive infinitum esse ita evinco. Omni ente finito potest aliud esse perfectius & majus. Deo nihil potest esse perfectius & majus. Ergo Deus non est ens finitum. QUARTO, Deus habet omnem entis perfectionem, quia absolutum primum, unde caetera omnia dependent, necessario perfectione sua excedit reliqua omnia entia. Ergo omnem eorum perfectionem eminentiori modo in se continet, et potentia quae numquam ita exhauriri possunt ut non novas rerum species & perfectiones depromere possint.
